source.title: CURIOUS: Intrinsically Motivated Modular Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning
source.venue: Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR)

confidence_rationale: Well-cited ICML paper from the group whose work ARC-073's notes already cite, and the closest computational instantiation of the claim's proposed signal. Marked mixed rather than supports because the agent's LP-driven attention explicitly RETURNS to goal regions whose performance decays -- saturation is demonstrated to be non-terminal, which is the single most consequential qualification of ARC-073's exit criterion. Confidence 0.62: high relevance, simulation-only, and the global-exit half of the claim is untested here rather than supported.
failure_signatures: Absolute learning progress is used, not signed LP, precisely so that a module whose performance is DECAYING is re-selected. A REE exit rule keyed on |d(PE)/dt| < threshold across all regions can therefore fire on a transient plateau and close a play episode that would have resumed producing world-model learning.

CURIOUS implements no transition to a non-exploratory mode at all: LP-based selection reallocates attention WITHIN exploration and never terminates it. The 'across all goal regions -> exit play' half of ARC-073 has no instantiation in the paper it is most naturally read as resting on.

LP is estimated over a sliding window with epsilon-greedy selection; the estimator is noisy, so the threshold test is a statistical decision with a false-positive rate that ARC-073 does not currently specify.

mapping.source_claim_statement: An agent facing many goals of heterogeneous difficulty can build its own curriculum by biasing goal selection toward the modules with the highest ABSOLUTE learning progress, estimated over a sliding window and sampled epsilon-greedily. This makes the agent focus on achievable goals first, ignore impossible or distracting goal spaces (whose LP stays at zero), and return to goals whose competence is decaying.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-073 proposes that play persists while learning progress is being produced and ends when |d(PE)/dt| falls below play_lp_saturation_threshold for all reachable regions. CURIOUS is the working demonstration that the first half of that is computable and useful: an LP estimate per goal region does discriminate mastered regions, unlearnable regions, and regions still yielding progress, and steering on it beats a uniform curriculum. This directly supports REE's plan to monitor a rolling LP estimate during play as a GoalConfig-parameterised signal. The second half fares worse. CURIOUS uses absolute LP by design, because a region whose LP has decayed to zero is not finished with -- forgetting makes it productive again later. Saturation in this system is a local, reversible, per-region state, not a global terminal one, and the paper never exits exploration.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Simulation in a robotic manipulation environment with a small, hand-specified set of goal modules; nothing about episode-level mode switching, homeostatic drive, or an embodied agent with a real task to return to. Reading CURIOUS as support for ARC-073's TRANSITION criterion over-reads it -- it supports the saturation SIGNAL and is silent-to-negative on saturation as a terminal condition. The 'reachable PE regions' quantifier in the claim also has no counterpart here: CURIOUS's module set is given, whereas REE would have to define what the reachable set is at the moment the test is applied.
mapping.source_context: Modular Goal Fetch Arm simulation; modular UVFA with hindsight experience replay; automated curriculum via absolute learning progress over a sliding window.

confidence_components.notes: Transfer risk is comparatively low because this is an artificial-agent result being transferred to another artificial agent -- the usual animal-to-machine hazard does not apply. Mapping fidelity is the binding constraint: the paper instantiates the signal ARC-073 wants but not the decision ARC-073 makes with it.
